purpose: Visual detection of Mobile Bay Jubilee development, nearshore contact and biological hypoxia response from owner waterfront camera imagery.
core_principles: Report only what is visibly supported.
Never infer dissolved oxygen directly from water color or appearance.
A Jubilee may begin offshore before animals reach the beach.
Bottom-dwelling animals appearing at or near the surface are more diagnostic than ordinary pelagic fish activity.
Multiple species responding abnormally is substantially stronger evidence than a single species.
Repeated activity over sequential frames is substantially stronger than an isolated splash.
Absence of visible animals is only negative evidence when detectability and relevant field of view are adequate.

If darkness, glare or resolution prevents a biological target from being resolved, report that target as unclear rather than none_visible; overall biological absence must be unclear rather than none when detectability is low.
Anonymous human search behavior is a soft detection/precursor signal, not Jubilee confirmation; never identify people or track identities.
Artificial lights, rain, wakes, insects, glare, debris and normal baitfish activity are important confounders.

shrimp: shrimp visibly popping or flicking at the surface
multiple discrete shrimp-like surface pops or rings
dense shrimp crowding immediately below or at the surface
shrimp concentrated unusually shallow against shoreline, dock or structure
fish_respiratory_stress: fish with mouths repeatedly breaking the surface
groups of fish appearing to gulp at the surface
local behavior sometimes described as smoking
fish holding at the surface rather than swimming normally
fish appearing lethargic, sluggish, disoriented or unusually easy to approach
dense fish compression at shoreline or structure
fish_surface_activity: repeated splashes with biological shape or trajectory
unusual dense fish schooling immediately at the surface
small fish showing widespread surface unrest
crabs: blue crabs swimming at the water surface
crabs making jerky or abnormal movements at the top of the water column
crabs with backs, claws or appendages breaking the surface
crabs climbing stumps, rocks, bulkheads or docks
crabs attempting to leave the water
bottom_fauna: flounder visible away from normal bottom concealment
hogchokers or other flatfish floating or unusually exposed
stingrays unusually shallow or near the surface
eels moving onto sand or shoreline
other normally demersal animals displaced into surface water
spatial_behavior: animals concentrated along a dock, piling line, stump line or bulkhead
dense biological band along water edge
offshore surface aggregation of normally bottom-associated animals
surface aggregation extending across more than one part of the frame
birds: dense coordinated feeding over one water area
birds feeding over independently visible fish or shrimp activity
human_response: people unexpectedly walking a normally quiet shoreline before dawn with lights while looking at the water
people using nets, gigs, baskets or buckets at dawn
people actively collecting shrimp, fish or crabs
slow clustered or sustained search behavior rather than ordinary transit
rapid increase in waterfront activity consistent with independent Jubilee evidence

artificial_light: fish gathered directly under fish lights
weather: rain drops producing repeated surface rings
heavy rain producing apparent boiling surface

montrose_shoreline: Primary 437 Village nearshore-contact and detectability view.
Looks directly at the swash zone/waterline and the sandy beach of 437 plus immediate neighboring beach segments north and south.
Old cedar stumps in the shallow water are fixed high-value biological reference structures; crabs climbing them or leaving the water would be a strong Jubilee-consistent sign.
Ordinary predawn beach foot traffic is uncommon because public access is limited, so people with lights looking at the water or dawn searchers with nets/gigs are unusually informative soft signals.
The road and parking are not visible; do not infer vehicle counts from this camera.

In full darkness the scene is generally too dark for reliable biology or waterline negatives. Bright moving lights/illuminated people may still be observable, but unresolved biology must be unclear. Increase direct biology emphasis at first usable light.
montrose_pier_bird: Looks primarily over very shallow water roughly 150+ feet offshore; water near the pier end is approximately 3 feet deep or less, tide dependent.
High value for early shallow-water fish/crab surface aggregation, bird feeding response and water-surface state.
Supporting view, not a substitute for direct shoreline contact in montrose_shoreline.
Same Montrose owner site cluster as the other two Montrose cameras and not an independent Jubilee confirmation.
montrose_pier_boat: Looks primarily over very shallow water roughly 150+ feet offshore; water near the pier end is approximately 3 feet deep or less, tide dependent.
High value for shallow-water surface disturbance, fish aggregation, shrimp popping and crab surface activity.
Supporting view, not a substitute for direct shoreline contact in montrose_shoreline.
Same Montrose owner site cluster as the other two Montrose cameras and not an independent Jubilee confirmation.
pcl_e2_bay_mouth: Runtime label is Point Clear E2 Down the Marina.
Owner-confirmed view looks approximately due west from the Point Clear site down the marina/inlet and onto Mobile Bay.
Useful for marina/Bay surface state, birds, visible biological activity, anonymous people/lights when resolvable and broad transport context.
It is not a close beach or swash-zone view; any shoreline cue is partial/distant, so absence cannot be generalized to Point Clear beaches.
Same Point Clear owner site cluster as E2 Back Deck and E3 Bay Mouth and not an independent Jubilee confirmation.
pcl_e2_back_deck: Owner-confirmed view overlooks the Point Clear marina toward the northwest.
Treat this as a marina-water supporting view rather than a direct beach or swash-zone camera.
Useful for marina surface activity, fish/shrimp/crab behavior around structures, birds, people/lights when resolvable and local water-surface state.
A clean frame can support absence only for biological activity that this marina field of view could actually resolve; do not generalize it to Point Clear beaches or open Bay.
Same Point Clear owner site cluster as the other Point Clear cameras and not an independent Jubilee confirmation.
pcl_e3_bay_mouth: Owner-confirmed view looks over the Point Clear marina toward the southeast.
Treat this as a marina-water supporting view rather than an open-Bay or direct beach camera.
Useful for marina surface activity, biological concentration around marina structures, birds and people/lights when resolvable.
A clean frame cannot establish absence on Point Clear beaches or across open Mobile Bay.
Same Point Clear owner site cluster as the other Point Clear cameras and not an independent Jubilee confirmation.

very_high_value: crabs climbing out of water or up cedar stumps
flounder, eel or stingray displaced abnormally shallow
multiple normally bottom-associated taxa simultaneously at surface
high_value: offshore surface aggregation of crabs or normally bottom-associated fish
supporting: unusual sustained predawn shoreline search with lights at the low-access 437 beach

strong: multiple independent biological classes show abnormal hypoxia-consistent behavior
clear crustacean or bottom-fauna displacement plus abnormal fish surface behavior
clear repeated abnormal activity corroborated across sequential frames
moderate: one highly diagnostic bottom-fauna signal is clearly visible
multiple shrimp surface pops with adequate visibility and no rain confounder
multiple crabs swimming at surface or climbing structures
clear fish gulping or widespread abnormal surface holding
weak_possible: multiple fish jumps without respiratory-stress behavior
bird feeding without visible biological confirmation
unusual human searching without visible biological confirmation
none: no abnormal biological behavior visible when detectability is moderate or high and the relevant field of view is adequate
unclear: darkness/glare/occlusion prevents the relevant target from being resolved

negative_evidence_rule: No visible activity may reduce visual Jubilee likelihood only when detectability is moderate or high and the camera field of view is capable of observing the relevant biological signal. Poor visibility, darkness, an offshore-only field of view or uncalibrated geometry must be UNKNOWN/unclear rather than negative evidence.
temporal_rule: A change across sequential images from normal to increasing surface activity, shrimp popping, fish gulping, crustacean displacement or shoreline concentration is more diagnostic than the same feature in a single frame. Human lights/searching require motion/persistence across frames when possible.
single_frame_warning: Shrimp popping, fish jumping, gulping, human searching and animal movement are temporal behaviors. A still frame can miss them. A negative single-frame result should not strongly suppress probability when these behaviors are the target.
